title: Finite Q3 common-word OS Gram/KMS context Cauchy stress
question: For actual finite d=3 Q3 Hamiltonians on nested path volumes and registered shape controls, do identical local half-period OS words have a source-fixed, volume-Cauchy Gram/KMS envelope, or does finite context dependence remain visible?
method: Reconstruct the manifest-defined d=3 Q3 onsite quartic and nonlinear bond matrices on path2, path3, path4, path5, bond2, square4 and grid2x3 with chi=1, r=-1, g=3/5, c=3/5 and lambda=1/10; validate edge bounds, uniqueness, and the fixed common source site 0.

Diagonalize each finite H and form T(s)=exp(-sH/hbar) in a shifted energy basis. For the same source-0 q- and p-character descriptors, use beta=0.25,0.5 and two positive half-period times tau/beta in every context.

Compute the normalized Hilbert-Schmidt OS Gram G_ij=Tr(F_i^*F_j)/Z, compare it with the reflected transfer trace formula, and require finite positive spectra, positive diagonals, and reflection agreement.
Compute W_qp(s)=Tr(T(beta*hbar-s) A_q T(s) A_p)/Z and W_pq(beta*hbar-s) for three interior thermal fractions; require the finite cyclic/KMS residual below 1e-9.

For path2->path3->path4->path5, compare identical descriptor Gram matrices and thermal words at adjacent volumes. Run an independent non-importing reconstruction and an integrated verifier with Lean R247 and explicit QFT scope firewalls.
decision_reason: The finite common-word comparison is reproducible and exposes nonzero context dependence while the declared path deltas decrease rapidly with volume: at beta=0.25 the maximum adjacent Gram/KMS context delta is 2.072876512015931e-05, 5.170797467979327e-08, and 1.3494971806693457e-10 for path2->path3, path3->path4, and path4->path5; at beta=0.5 the corresponding maxima are 1.151259587772735e-04, 2.474974451160961e-06, and 5.390589497000776e-08. This advances the finite QFT-facing target by identifying a concrete boundary-to-source decay pattern, but the finite sequence is not a source/volume-uniform analytic Cauchy theorem and cannot identify a common OS carrier or Hamiltonian limit.
finding: Primary 171/171 and independent 171/171 assertions pass over 7 finite contexts, 14 OS Gram rows, 42 thermal rows, and 6 adjacent path comparisons; the integrated verifier passes 16/16 with Lean R247 PASS. Every finite Gram matrix is positive within the declared tolerance, the reflected trace agrees with the Hilbert-Schmidt form, and every thermal word satisfies finite cyclicity. The maximum adjacent context delta is 1.151259587772735e-04 and the minimum is 1.3494971806693457e-10. For beta=0.25 the path maximum-delta sequence is nonincreasing, and the beta=0.5 sequence is also nonincreasing in the recorded comparisons. The nonzero deltas are retained as evidence that finite context dependence has not been assumed away.
next_action: Use the observed path decay only as a target for an analytic source-to-boundary estimate with explicit volume and degree constants. Compare that estimate against the direct D/delta-D route; if the bound cannot be made uniform in source, volume, cutoff and beta, append the resulting route-local obstruction before any common-alpha or Hamiltonian-to-OS promotion.

adversarial_review.check: Only source-0 q/p character descriptors and identical beta/time grids are compared; no finite Hamiltonians are asserted equal under an unproved tensor embedding.
All transfer factors use exp(-sH/hbar), period beta*hbar and the half-period reflection convention; real-time signs are not mixed into the Euclidean comparison.
Adjacent finite deltas are reported as diagnostics. Their decrease is not promoted to a uniform thermodynamic Cauchy bound.
The path contexts add a far-boundary edge, but no locality or clustering estimate is assumed to suppress its effect at source 0.
The numerical Gram spectrum and direct reflected trace are checked in every declared context and beta; positivity is kept finite-dimensional.
The independent lane reconstructs oscillator tensors, Q3 terms, spectral transfer, Gram, KMS and context comparisons without importing the primary lane.
R247 checks exact rational finite Gibbs normalization/commutation and conditional transfer scope; dense Q3 matrices and context deltas remain Python evidence.

Finite context decay does not construct a common OS carrier, prove source/volume/cutoff/beta uniformity, establish common alpha, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, a GNS gap, continuum removal, C6, Sector A or Pre-A.

qft_interface.closed: For the seven declared finite contexts, identical source-0 transfer-word descriptors give positive finite OS Gram matrices and finite thermal cyclicity, with explicit adjacent path context deltas and an independent/Lean crosscheck.
qft_interface.open: A source/volume/cutoff/beta-uniform analytic Cauchy estimate, common-word exhaustion embedding, direct D/delta-D convergence, common core, one common alpha, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, GNS gap, continuum and physical TECT gates remain open.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Auxiliary C6/Q3 finite evidence only; no heat_root_incidence, canonical A1/R-192 production owner, physical-empty reference, Sector-A closure or Pre-A closure is supplied.

boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite d=3 common-word context comparison. It is not a common OS carrier theorem, thermodynamic limit, common-alpha construction, mass-gap proof, continuum result, or QFT/Clay closure.
no_overclaim: This package proves only finite matrix transfer-word positivity, finite cyclicity, and explicit context-delta diagnostics for the declared graphs. It does not prove a thermodynamic OS measure, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, source/volume-uniform Cauchy convergence, a common alpha, a GNS mass gap, continuum removal, C6, Sector A, Pre-A or a Clay result.
